question: If I will reach home before the prayer time ends, should I shorten on the road or pray in full at home?
answer:
The next point here is: suppose you are traveling and you are going to reach home within the time of the salah, so you have the option. To give a simple example: maghrib comes in, let's say simplistically, at 7 p.m., and you will be home by 6 p.m. So you know that you will be able to pray dhuhr and asr at home, and you know, I can stop on this road and pray, or at a masjid on the street or whatever in the other area I can pray. You have an option. What should you do?

Response: **it is completely up to you.** The Shari'ah is neutral as to which one you should prefer. If you choose to stop, you are still a musafir, so you will pray two and two. However, if you get home, you are no longer a musafir, and even though you are forgiven for the qasr — as we're going to come to in a while — now you must pray four and four.

So if you stop on the road, even though you can make it home in time, it is permissible. Why? Because Allah 'azza wa jall has linked qasr with safar, and if you are in safar, qasr is allowed. And there is no guarantee; anything can happen. Your car can break down, a traffic jam; there is no guarantee that you will get there exactly on time. So you make an assumption, and therefore the Shari'ah does not hold you accountable for your assumption. If you're a musafir, you do qasr, and if you get home, you no longer do qasr. So that option is up to you.
